rationale: Use an independent, server-rendered Python client for local demonstrations so existing services remain the authority for business state, authorization, and persistence. A visible prototype notice, plain-text service ownership and failure details, and synthetic server-side personas separated by role make the prototype honest and didactic. Bounded single-worker in-memory sessions and fixed opt-in terminal load scenarios meet the presentation need without adding a gateway, shared domain library, database, broker consumer, or general-purpose load generator. The scenarios' fixed pool contains exactly twenty unique, unscoped participants, is enabled consistently in the web client and identity mock, is rejected when malformed or oversized, and keeps tokens server-side. Presentation code is outside the domain-core mutation-score denominator, but remains subject to focused adapter, security, and browser tests; existing domain gates are unchanged.
invariants: Existing services and contracts remain authoritative for business rules, protected operations, and owned data.
The presentation client does not add a generic gateway, shared domain import, database, broker consumer, or independent domain state.
Every page identifies the prototype, and failures name the owning service and correlation id rather than being hidden or replaced by fabricated content.
Synthetic personas are not authentication; protected requests preserve backend identity validation, authorization, and participant isolation.
Session identifiers are opaque; server-side session state is bounded and expiring, and the application runs as one worker/replica without durable or multi-worker session assumptions.
Mutations use existing APIs and idempotency behavior; uncertain outcomes are never converted into fabricated success or failure.
The load scenarios are opt-in, finite, fixed-scope, resource-bounded, and use existing service APIs and synthetic identities.
Presentation-layer mutation exclusions do not waive adapter, security, browser, or regression tests and do not weaken the existing minimum 95 percent domain mutation gate.
